title: Add transactional owner visit creation and inquiry confirmation core
requirements: Add an explicitly injected domain service for future authenticated owner HTTP handlers; it receives a trusted owner UUID, an injected Engine, an injected non-empty HMAC secret and positive digest-key version. This task exposes no route and must not compose a production runtime.

Implement create_planned_visit for the accepted POST /api/v1/admin/visits semantic payload: service_id, UTC start_at and duration_minutes (null or positive integer). It validates an active service, creates a PLANNED visit at version 1, and returns a deterministic result containing command_id and the created visit id/version/status.

Implement confirm_inquiry for the accepted CONFIRM semantic: inquiry_id, expected inquiry version, a complete expected version map containing the target PLANNED visit, and payload visit_id. It accepts only NEW or NEGOTIATING inquiries with no current participation, creates one current participation, moves the inquiry to CONFIRMED, increments both inquiry and visit versions, and returns command_id plus the changed inquiry and visit IDs/versions. It does not silently replace an existing current participation; such a request returns PARTICIPATION_CONFLICT for the later explicit MOVE workflow.

Both operations implement the accepted CRM idempotency protocol using operation_receipts: owner UUID + method + canonical path are the scope; normalized semantic payload is digested with the injected secret; identical completed replays return the original result without new mutation; a changed payload gives IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH; tombstoned/absent result gives RESULT_EXPIRED. Errors before acceptance do not consume a key. The visit creation canonical path is /api/v1/admin/visits and the confirmation canonical path is /api/v1/admin/inquiries/{inquiry_id}/commands.

For a new command, acquire business_write_guard first, then lock and compare every existing object against the supplied expected version before mutation. Missing expected inquiry/visit version is EXPECTED_VERSION_REQUIRED; a mismatch is VERSION_CONFLICT; invalid IDs, input, status or unavailable plan are a typed safe command error and leave all business tables unchanged. Confirmation must not require payment, total price or prepayment.

For each accepted first execution, store the receipt result and write an OWNER change_event linked to the receipt. Visit creation links an event_visits row; confirmation links both event_inquiries and event_visits rows. Record only safe structured before/after identifiers, status and versions in changes. Do not create notification delivery jobs in this narrow core because recipient policy and HTTP dispatch remain separate tasks.

Add isolated synthetic PostgreSQL integration tests for visit creation, active-service/input validation, confirmation from NEW and NEGOTIATING, exact expected-version behaviour, no implicit replacement, idempotent replay and mismatch, atomic rejection, receipt/event links and no payment prerequisite. Tests create isolated random databases and never read a local .env or use a configured source database.

Do not add HTTP handlers, session/CSRF changes, manual inquiry entry, update/move/complete/cancel commands, migration changes, payment mutations, notification delivery, frontend assets, bot adapters, secrets or external calls.
acceptance: The first owner command core can create an empty planned group visit and explicitly confirm one eligible incoming inquiry without treating payment as a prerequisite.
Retries are safe and concurrency/version conflicts do not produce partial state or duplicate audit history.
Focused isolated PostgreSQL tests, scope and whitespace checks pass.

shared_paths_approval.reason: Accepted narrow transactional owner command core whose future HTTP composition is deliberately deferred, avoiding overlap with the independent calendar read task.
